text:
Jackson Blake turned 23 in August with a Stanley Cup ring from last spring, and Carolina has handed him a bigger job to match. He's playing 17:55 a night, up from 16:30, and he's on the ice for 83% of the Hurricanes' power-play chances after 40% last season. The result: 18 points in 18 games and an active eight-game point streak (three goals, seven assists).

The odd part is that the assists are carrying him. He has four goals on 7.4 expected goals, the quality of his chances, and he's shooting 8.7%. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the home-plate area in front of the net at an 88th-percentile rate last season, so the looks aren't new. Goals usually follow.

There's some help baked in, too. The Hurricanes have scored 3.3 more goals than expected with him on the ice, and Evolving-Hockey noted his teammates rank among the league's strongest. Our projection puts him around 67 points. The Hockey Writers say he's approaching star status; we'd want to see the shooting catch up before we say it ourselves.
headline: Jackson Blake's assists are running ahead of his goals
